name: Biological NTLA-2002
summary: NTLA-2002 is lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), Intellia's in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 edit of KLKB1 in the liver, delivered by lipid nanoparticle as a single 50 mg outpatient IV infusion to prevent hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks. The pivotal trial is HAELO (NCT06634420): a randomised 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 in 80 patients aged 16 and over with C1-inhibitor-deficient (type 1 or 2) HAE. At weeks 5 to 28, the monthly attack rate was 0.26 on lonvo-z against 2.10 on placebo, 87% lower (NEJM 2026, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2600931). The BLA has Priority Review with a PDUFA date of 2027-03-10 (8-K 0001193125-26-385194). Price anchor: Casgevy, the only marketed CRISPR/Cas9 therapy, at its $2.2mm one-time list price as the book carries it. That is about 3.1 years of the more than $700,000 a year that Intellia says long-term prophylaxis costs, the basis payers use to price one-time therapies. The discount is Zolgensma's measured CMS reimbursement against list. Uptake anchor: Orladeyo, the last novel prophylaxis to launch in HAE, whose FY2025 US revenue implies about 18.7% of the US treated-HAE population on therapy in its fifth year. Lonvo-z is set to reach the same share of its eligible pool by year five. Intellia keeps all of it: the 10-Q calls lonvo-z wholly owned. Regeneron's 25% share covers nex-z (ATTR), not this asset. A low- to mid-single-digit royalty to Caribou is not netted.

therapy_mode.source: Intellia 8-K 2026-09-08 (0001193125-26-385194, EX-99.1): HAELO 'was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a one-time 50 milligram dose of lonvo-z'; Cohn DM et al., NEJM 2026, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2600931 (PMID 42294842): 'a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z (at a dose of 50 mg)'
therapy_mode.note: One infusion, not repeated. It is billed once, so each year's treated patients are that year's revenue. The book models its other one-time CRISPR therapy (Casgevy) and the one-time CAR T seeds the same way
therapy_mode.check: 8-K 0001193125-26-385194 EX-99.1 (book filing_sections) reads 'designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a one-time 50 milligram dose of lonvo-z'. PubMed abstract of PMID 42294842 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2600931) reads 'a single intravenous infusion of lonvo-z (at a dose of 50 mg)'. In forecast.py the one_time branch bills each year's patients once, so one_time is the right mode.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py seed Exagamglogene autotemcel: list_price_per_patient 2.2 mm USD, 'Vertex, Dec 2023 launch price' (Casgevy, the only marketed CRISPR/Cas9 therapy). Cross-check on HAE prophylaxis: Intellia management said payers value one-time therapies as a multiple of the average annual cost of long-term prophylaxis (LTP), which 'can exceed $700,000 annually'. No price has been set, and Intellia expects premium pricing (MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 'Intellia Eyes Lonvo-z Launch as HAE PDUFA Nears, TTR Study Advances', finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/intellia-eyes-lonvo-z-launch-040202231.html; read from the search summary, page not opened). Commercial plans paid a mean $395,845 per patient-year for LTP drugs (Tachdjian R et al., World Allergy Organ J 2026;19(7):101399, doi:10.1016/j.waojou.2026.101399, PMID 42318594; IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, 328 patients)
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the anchor. Intellia has not set a price. Casgevy is the closest published price for the same modality: a one-time CRISPR/Cas9 therapy that replaces lifelong treatment. $2.2mm is 3.1 years of the more than $700,000 a year that management cites for LTP, and 5.6 years of the $395,845 commercial plans actually paid per patient-year. Case for higher: management expects premium pricing. Hemgenix, a one-time gene therapy that replaces hemophilia B prophylaxis, lists at $3.5mm, about 5 years of $700,000. Lonvo-z has no conditioning regimen and no hospital stay, and 62% of HAELO patients were attack-free and therapy-free for six months (8-K 0001193125-26-385194). Case for lower: HAE is rarely fatal, management says payer resistance rises at higher multiples and step edits are possible, durability past a few years is unproven, and newer LTPs (garadacimab, donidalorsen) add price competition. Casgevy's $2.2mm is carried by the book from a workbook cell; it matches Vertex's published December 2023 list price
list_price_per_patient.check: Anchor: lookup.py seed Exagamglogene autotemcel carries list_price_per_patient 2.2 mm USD ('Vertex, Dec 2023 launch price'). A web search confirms Casgevy's US WAC at $2.2mm (Bloomberg via StreetInsider; BioPharma Dive, Dec 2023). Checked against a published HAE prophylaxis price: Orladeyo's WAC was $485,004 a year at its 2020 launch and $48,487.92 per 28-day pack from 9 Jan 2026 (BioCryst 8-K via search summary), $630,343 a year at 13 packs. So $2.2mm is 3.49 years of Orladeyo's 2026 WAC, 3.14 years of the more than $700,000 a year Intellia cites for LTP (MarketBeat via Yahoo, search summary: 'Intellia has not set a price for lonvo-z', and payers price one-time therapies as multiples of LTP), and 5.56 years of the $395,845 plan-paid LTP cost per patient-year (PMID 42318594 abstract, which confirms the figure and the 328 patients). No ICER or other published price exists for lonvo-z or any HAE gene therapy (searched). The 62% attack-free and therapy-free figure and the outpatient setting are confirmed in the 8-K. Hemgenix's $3.5mm was not re-checked; it appears only in the note. A labelled judgement whose inputs hold.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec, one-time IV gene therapy): the CMS reimbursement had fallen to $1.36mm by 2022 against a $2.125mm list price, which BioSpace calls 'nearly a 40% discount' ('Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?', biospace.com/who-s-paying-for-million-dollar-gene-therapies; read from the search summary). 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36
gross_to_net_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. The anchor is a list price (WAC), so neither house Medicare convention applies. The discount has to be sourced, and Zolgensma is the one-time gene therapy with a measured net-of-discount CMS figure against its list. Direction checked: 0.36 is the share off list, so net is $1.408mm per course. Case for lower: HAE patients are mostly commercially insured adults, while SMA infants carry a large Medicaid share. The Medicaid statutory minimum rebate is 23.1% of AMP and applies to Medicaid units only. The book's Casgevy seed assumes about 18% ($1.8mm net on $2.2mm, a workbook estimate). Case for higher: if $1.36mm is CMS's Part B payment limit (106% of ASP), the ASP-based discount is 1 - (1.36/1.06)/2.125 = 0.396
gross_to_net_pct.check: The BioSpace search summary ('Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?', July 2024) reads: 'By 2022, the reimbursement for Zolgensma dropped to $1.36 million per claim, nearly a 40% discount from its list price, according to CMS', with CMS spending about $87.25mm on some 63 treatments. Zolgensma's $2.125mm list is confirmed by BioSpace's approval headline. 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36. The direction is right: 0.36 is the share off list, so net = 2.2 x 0.64 = $1.408mm. Minor: $87.25mm / 63 = $1.385mm, which gives 0.348. Checked against HAE: no HAE prophylaxis gross-to-net is published. I searched BioCryst releases and calls and found only a volume effect, 84% of Orladeyo patients on paid drug in Q1 2025, up from 73.5% at the end of 2024. The $1.408mm net is 2.23 years of Orladeyo's 2026 WAC ($630,343) and 3.56 years of the $395,845 plan-paid LTP cost, inside the multiples-of-LTP range Intellia describes. The researcher labels it a judgement and states the case for lower (a commercial HAE population against Medicaid-heavy SMA; the Casgevy seed at about 18%), so it stands. The 'CMS' dataset behind $1.36mm is not named in the summary, and if it is Medicaid, a per-claim figure can sit below list for reasons other than discount. That argues for less off list, not more.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: one infusion, not repeated (8-K 0001193125-26-385194; NEJM 2026, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2600931)
discontinuation_pct.note: Set so the engine never carries a treated stock forward in either mode. one_time mode ignores it. Re-dosing is not modelled
discontinuation_pct.check: forecast.py: the one_time branch sets treated = total_patients and reads discontinuation_pct only in the chronic branch, so 1.0 is inert here and harmless if the mode changes. The single-infusion source is confirmed (8-K 0001193125-26-385194; PMID 42294842).

cogs_per_patient.source: none found. Searched Intellia's 10-K FY2025 (0001193125-26-076550) and its 2026 10-Qs (0001193125-26-215740, 0001193125-26-337952) in the book's filing_sections, and the web: Intellia discloses no cost of goods or manufacturing cost for lonvo-z
cogs_per_patient.note: Left null. Intellia has no product revenue, so it has no cost-of-sales ratio for the BMS-986353 and VLA15 method (company ratio times net price). The book's Casgevy figure (0.75 mm, a workbook estimate) is for autologous ex vivo manufacture and does not transfer to an LNP-delivered mRNA and guide RNA. WARNING for the company step: the engine charges cogs_pct x revenue in one_time mode when this field is null. Intellia has no company rows in the book, so unless that step supplies cogs_pct or a per-course figure, the build charges no cost of goods at all
cogs_per_patient.check: Null accepted. No per-course cost is disclosed: a regex over Intellia's FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q in the book's filing_sections finds no 'cost of goods', 'cost of sales', 'manufacturing cost' or 'gross margin' wording, and no web source gives one. forecast.py lines 561-566: with cogs_per_patient null in one_time mode, cogs = cogs_pct x revenue, so the company step's cost of sales share applies once Intellia's cost block is built. The Casgevy 0.75 is an ex vivo workbook estimate ('est. 500k-1mm manufacturing cost', lookup.py seed) and rightly not carried.

forecast_start_year.source: FDA accepted the BLA with Priority Review, PDUFA date 2027-03-10 (8-K 0001193125-26-385194). Intellia plans a US launch in the first half of 2027 (10-Q 0001193125-26-337952). HAELO (NCT06634420) primary completion 2026-02-10, actual (book trials table)
forecast_start_year.note: 2027 is the first full year after the current one, and launch is not later. It is a partial year, since approval can come no earlier than 10 March. The ramp starts at 8.5% of peak in year 0, which absorbs part of that. Case for 2028: an advisory committee or a CMC question for the first in vivo CRISPR BLA could push the action date
forecast_start_year.check: 8-K 0001193125-26-385194: PDUFA target action date 10 March 2027, Priority Review. Q2 2026 10-Q 0001193125-26-337952 MD&A: 'we plan to launch lonvo-z in the U.S. in the first half of 2027'. Book trials table: NCT06634420 primary completion 2026-02-10, actual; 80 enrolled. s_curve(0)/peak = 1/(1+exp(1.08 x 2.2)) = 0.085, matching the 8.5% stated. The same 8-K says the FDA 'is not currently planning to hold an advisory committee', which weakens the note's case for 2028. Amass TrialCore was unavailable (usage limit), so the book's trials row is the check.

exus_multiple.source: Orladeyo (berotralstat), BioCryst Q1 2025 results release (ir.biocryst.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biocryst-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results-and): 'Sales from the U.S. contributed 89.5 percent of global ORLADEYO net revenues in the first quarter of 2025'. 10.5 / 89.5 = 0.1173
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. Orladeyo is an HAE prophylaxis launched ex-US by a small US biotech, which is closest to Intellia's position. Intellia has disclosed only a US launch and no ex-US partner. The figure is one quarter, read from the search summary and not opened. Case for higher: Takhzyro, launched by a global pharma, sells a larger share outside the US (not sourced here). Case for lower: European HTA bodies have been slow to reimburse one-time CRISPR and gene therapies at $2mm or more, and Intellia may not launch ex-US in the forecast window at all. The engine applies this multiple to the pool and prices ex-US patients at the US net price
exus_multiple.check: Search summary of BioCryst's Q1 2025 release: 'Sales from the U.S. contributed 89.5 percent of global ORLADEYO net revenues in the first quarter of 2025'. 10.5 / 89.5 = 0.11732. The judgement is labelled with its case against. Context: BioCryst's preliminary FY2025 release gives $601mm global and $563mm excluding European revenue, since Europe was divested in 2025. The FY2025 non-US share is therefore at least 6.3% and includes Europe for part of the year, consistent with the Q1 figure. forecast.py scales both the pool and the inflow by (1 + exus_multiple).

economics_share.source: Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06) and 10-Q for Q1 2026 (0001193125-26-215740), MD&A: 'Lonvo-z is a wholly owned, investigational in vivo CRISPR-based therapeutic candidate'. Same filing: nex-z (ATTR) is the Regeneron Co/Co, where 'Regeneron shares in approximately 25% of worldwide development costs and commercial profits for the ATTR program'. Royalty: Intellia 10-K FY2024 (0000950170-25-029007), collaboration note, refers to 'the Company's existing low- to mid-single-digit royalty obligations under a license agreement with Caribou'
economics_share.note: DISCREPANCY with the brief: Regeneron holds no share of lonvo-z. The filings call it wholly owned, and Regeneron's roughly 25% applies to the ATTR programme (nex-z) only. 1.0 is a ceiling. Intellia pays Caribou a low- to mid-single-digit royalty on net sales of products under the UC/Vienna CRISPR-Cas9 sublicence, and lonvo-z is a Cas9 product. The house netting is (margin - royalty) / margin, and it is not applied: the filing gives only a range, and Intellia has no company cost rows in the book to set the margin. At a margin m and royalty r, the company step should set (m - r) / m. The Broad Institute patent dispute could add a licence cost; none is sourced
economics_share.check: Wholly owned is confirmed verbatim in both 2026 10-Qs, book filing_sections MD&A: Q1 0001193125-26-215740 and Q2 0001193125-26-337952 read 'Lonvo-z is a wholly owned, investigational in vivo CRISPR-based therapeutic candidate'. The 8-Ks of 2025-11-06 and 2026-02-26 say the same. Q2 10-Q: 'Regeneron shares in approximately 25% of worldwide development costs and commercial profits for the ATTR program', so nex-z only. Caribou: FY2024 10-K 0000950170-25-029007, collaboration note (Regeneron section), reads 'incorporate the Company's existing low- to mid-single-digit royalty obligations under a license agreement with Caribou'. The FY2025 10-K sections in the book do not repeat the rate. The 2026 10-Qs say Intellia may pay 'royalties based on our revenues, including sales revenues of our products, utilizing the technologies ... sublicensed from third parties, including Caribou', so the royalty reaches lonvo-z (a Cas9 product under the UC/Vienna sublicence). ROYALTY TO NET: 0.01 of net sales. That is the bottom of 'low- to mid-single-digit', which the book reads as 1%, as the Adimanebart IV seed takes 'low single digits'. The company step sets economics_share = (m - 0.01) / m once Intellia's cost block fixes the margin m. 1.0 is the pre-royalty ownership share.

prevalence.source: Castaldo AJ et al., 'Establishing a hereditary angioedema prevalence for the United States using a large administrative claims database', Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol 2025;135(3):303-310, doi:10.1016/j.anai.2025.05.018 (PMID 40414286; IQVIA PharMetrics Plus MedTech, adjusted for Medicare under-representation). Expert-panel-reviewed US HAE (all types, all ages) was 2.13 per 100,000 and 7,602 people in 2018, 2.03 and 7,275 in 2019, and 1.84 and 6,595 in 2020
prevalence.note: Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool 'Angioedema' returns nothing, and epidemiology.csv has no HAE line. This is the first HAE pool, so the next HAE seeds (donidalorsen, BMN 331) should reuse it. JUDGEMENT to take 2019, the last pre-pandemic year and the middle of the three expert-reviewed figures. The claims algorithm alone gives 8,694 to 9,559. Each patient needed at least one pharmacy claim for an HAE drug, so this is diagnosed and treated HAE, which suits a pool for a prescribed therapy. Intellia's '1 in 50,000' (8-K 0001193125-26-385194) implies about 6,800 in the US. The count includes HAE with normal C1-INH, which eligible_pct removes
prevalence.check: PubMed abstract, PMID 40414286 (Castaldo 2025, Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol 135(3):303-310): expert-panel estimates were 2.13 and 7,602 for 2018, 2.03 and 7,275 for 2019, 1.84 and 6,595 for 2020. The claims algorithm gave 9,559, 9,341 and 8,694. The algorithm requires at least one pharmacy claim for an HAE-indicated drug and covers all HAE types. The abstract says Medicare adjustment factors came from a sensitivity analysis but does not say whether the headline counts carry them; this does not change the value. Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool 'Angioedema' and 'Hereditary' return nothing, epidemiology.csv has no HAE line, and no other out/ or verified/ file names the indication. Intellia's 'one in 50,000' is confirmed in 8-K 0001193125-26-385194.

incidence.source: Congenital (autosomal dominant), so the inflow is demographic. US births 3,628,934 in 2024 (NVSR 75-02, Births: Final Data for 2024, as the book's PCV21 and MMRVNS seeds carry it), times Castaldo's 2019 rate of 2.03 per 100,000 (PMID 40414286): 73.7, rounded to 74
incidence.note: JUDGEMENT. It assumes each birth cohort carries HAE at the population's diagnosed rate and reaches the pool when it comes of age, the method the book's Lepodisiran and Olpasiran seeds use. The cohort turning 16 in 2027 was born in 2011 and was larger than 2024's (not quantified here). The engine also applies eligible_pct, which includes the age filter, to this inflow. Both effects understate it slightly. At about 1% of the pool a year, it matters only in the tail
incidence.check: The book carries 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (NVSR 75-02) on the PCV21 and MMRVNS seeds; x 2.03 / 100,000 (PMID 40414286) = 73.67, rounded to 74. The Lepodisiran and Olpasiran seeds use the same demographic-inflow method. In forecast.py the inflow is x eligible_pct: 74 x 0.831535 = 61.5 a year.

eligible_pct.source: Two filters from HAELO's entry criteria (NEJM 2026, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2600931: aged 16 or over, HAE with C1 inhibitor deficiency). (1) Type 1 or 2 (C1-INH deficient): 92.4% of 368 US patients in the Adelphi HAE Disease Specific Programme, 2021 (Anderson et al., 'Physician- and patient-reported outcomes by hereditary angioedema type', Allergy Asthma Proc 2024;45(4):247-254, doi:10.2500/aap.2024.45.240021, PMID 38982603). (2) Age: the pediatric treated cohort was 143 of 1,429 US HAE-treated patients (Tachdjian R et al., Allergy Asthma Proc 2020;41(3):172-182, doi:10.2500/aap.2020.41.200011, PMID 32375961), so 1 - 143/1,429 = 0.8999 are adults. 0.924 x 0.8999 = 0.831535
eligible_pct.note: Under-18 stands in for under-16, so the age filter slightly understates the eligible share. No severity filter: HAELO required investigator-confirmed attacks during a run-in after LTP washout (trial listings via search; no minimum count confirmed), and no marketed HAE prophylaxis label restricts by attack rate. Case for a lower value: in the sole-dispenser berotralstat dataset, 311 of 701 US patients had normal-C1-INH HAE (Davis-Lorton et al., Allergy Asthma Clin Immunol 2026, doi:10.1186/s13223-025-01005-x, PMID 41582175). In claims-treated HAE the normal-C1-INH share may therefore be well above Adelphi's 7.6%. At 30%, eligible falls to 0.63. Patients well controlled on current LTP may also not seek a permanent edit; the penetration anchor, not this field, carries that. Pool: 7,275 x 0.831535 = 6,049 US patients
eligible_pct.check: PMID 38982603 abstract (Anderson 2024): 368 patients, 92.4% HAE types I/II, 7.6% normal C1-INH. PMID 32375961 abstract (Tachdjian 2020): 1,429 treated, pediatric treated cohort n = 143. 0.924 x (1 - 143/1429) = 0.831535, and 7,275 x 0.831535 = 6,049. The label pool matches HAELO: PMID 42294842 enrolled patients 'aged 16 or older with hereditary angioedema with C1 inhibitor deficiency', and the 8-K says Type 1 or Type 2. The 2020 cohorts are 'nonexclusive', so some pediatric patients may also count as adults; like the under-18 proxy, this understates eligibility slightly. The case for lower is confirmed: PMID 41582175 (Davis-Lorton 2026) has 390 C1INH-deficient and 311 normal-C1INH berotralstat patients. A labelled judgement whose inputs hold.

untreated_carryover_pct.unit: share of untreated eligible patients still eligible the next year
untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.derive_new_patients default (the Zolgensma shape: a prevalent pool drawn down, with the tail converging on incidence)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. HAE is lifelong, and a patient not treated this year stays eligible. No survival deficit for treated HAE is sourced, so no death term is applied. Case against: deaths (asphyxiation is rare) and loss to follow-up shrink the pool slightly each year
untreated_carryover_pct.check: forecast.derive_new_patients defaults carryover to 1.0 (the Zolgensma shape). The judgement is labelled and its case against stated. The brief's stationary alternative, retention = 6,049.4 / (6,049.4 + 61.5) = 0.98993, was tested. The engine's untreated pool never outgrows its opening size here, because treatment (about 400 a year at peak) far exceeds the 61.5 inflow, which is why this was not corrected. At 0.98993 with the same p = 0.0828, treated patients over 10 years fall from 3,010 to 2,859 (-5%). Re-solving p to the same five-year target gives 0.0854, a year-6 peak of 407 against 418, and 2,925 over 10 years (-2.8%). A death exit of about 1% a year would be defensible: HAE is lifelong and Castaldo's measured count did not grow over 2018-2020. It moves value by only a few percent.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Incumbent: Orladeyo (berotralstat), the last novel-mechanism HAE prophylaxis, launched December 2020. FY2025 net revenue was $601mm (BioCryst preliminary FY2025 release, ir.biocryst.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biocryst-announces-preliminary-full-year-2025-orladeyor), with 89.5% US (Q1 2025 release, above): $537.9mm. Divided by the $395,845 commercial plans paid per LTP patient-year (Tachdjian 2026, PMID 42318594), that is 1,359 US patient-years on therapy, 18.7% of Castaldo's 7,275 treated HAE patients, in Orladeyo's fifth year. Solved through the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients, k 1.08, midpoint 2.2, pool 6,049, inflow 61.5 a year) so that lonvo-z has treated 18.7% of the eligible pool by the end of year 5: p = 0.0828. Treated patients run 43, 109, 225, 345 and 408 a year, peaking at 418 in year 6
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on Orladeyo's five-year share. Several steps are approximate. Revenue is net of rebates while $395,845 is the plan-paid amount, and 16% of Orladeyo patients were on free drug in Q1 2025 (search summary); both push the patient count up. Orladeyo users include normal-C1-INH patients, and its per-patient cost may exceed the all-LTP mean: berotralstat alone was about $312,559 per six months in persistent patients (Princic N et al., J Comp Eff Res 2025, doi:10.57264/cer-2024-0205, PMID 39976166), which gives 861 patient-years, an 11.8% share and p = 0.0511. The 2019 prevalence denominator predates later growth in treated HAE. Case for higher: 87% fewer attacks, 62% attack-free and therapy-free, and one treatment ends lifelong dosing. LTP churn is high: 12-month persistence was 58.7% in Komodo claims (Lumry W et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2026, doi:10.1186/s13023-026-04391-6, PMID 42157298), and Orladeyo took 257 of 499 LTP starts there. Case for lower: one-time gene therapies have launched slowly (the book's Casgevy seed peaks at 0.011), the edit is permanent, and management warns of payer step edits. New LTPs (garadacimab, donidalorsen, navenibart) are competing for the same switchers. Implied peak net revenue is about $588mm US ($657mm with ex-US) at the $1.408mm net price
penetration_peak_pct.check: Inputs: BioCryst's preliminary FY2025 Orladeyo net revenue of $601mm is confirmed (release of 12 Jan 2026; $563mm excluding Europe); the Q1 2025 US share of 89.5% and 84% of patients on paid drug are confirmed; $395,845 plan-paid LTP cost per patient-year is confirmed (PMID 42318594). 601 x 0.895 = 537.9; / 0.395845 = 1,358.9 patient-years; / 7,275 = 18.68%. Engine solve recomputed (k 1.08, midpoint 2.2, pool 6,049.4, inflow 61.5, carryover 1.0): p = 0.08282, treated 43, 109, 225, 345, 408, peaking at 418 in year 6. Implied peak net revenue: 418 x 1.408 = $588mm US, $657mm with ex-US. Alternatives recomputed: Princic (PMID 39976166 abstract) gives 373,010 - 60,451 = $312,559 per six months, so 860.5 patient-years, 11.83%, p = 0.0511. Lumry (PMID 42157298) has 58.7% 12-month persistence and 257 of 499 Orladeyo. One more case for lower that the note only touches: 311 of 701 berotralstat patients had normal C1-INH (PMID 41582175). Keeping only the C1-INH-deficient share, (1,358.9 x 390/701) / (7,275 x 0.924) = 11.2%, and p = 0.0485. A labelled judgement (a multiple of 1.0 on Orladeyo's five-year share) whose inputs and arithmetic hold.

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020-2024), k = 1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as carried by the MK-1045 and camizestrant seeds (lookup.py seed MK-1045) and used by the book's one-time CAR T seeds (AZD0120, BMS-986353)
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT to reuse it. The book has no HAE launch series. Orladeyo's revenue rose every year through its fifth year (to $437mm in FY2024 and $601mm in FY2025), which argues for a slower, later midpoint than a fitted oncology launch. Lonvo-z also needs site-of-care and payer set-up for an outpatient infusion
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Enhertu, Part B beneficiaries: 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 (2020-2024). lookup.py seed MK-1045 carries k = 1.08 and midpoint 2.2 from this fit, and the BMS-986353 seed carries both.
